Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
The actual diameter of a prokaryotic cell is 0.5m. An electron micrograph of the cell has a magnification of 50000. What is the diameter of the cell in the image?
The electron micrograph shows some cell structures. Some cell structures are listed.
ribosomes
mitochondria
plasmodesmata Which cell structures can be seen in the electron micrograph?

A student carried out tests for biological molecules on the same sample of milk. The tests and their results were as follows. ● Heating to 80C with Benedict’s solution gave a red colour. ● Boiling with acid, followed by neutralisation, then heating to 80C with Benedict’s solution also gave a red colour. ● Adding Biuret solution gave a purple colour. ● Adding iodine solution gave a yellow colour. Which biological molecules must be present in the milk?
Which row is correct for carbohydrates? monomer polymer macromolecule

options.A: fructose amylose cellulose

Which row shows a correct comparison between a phospholipid molecule and a triglyceride molecule? phospholipid molecule triglyceride molecule

options.A: contains a hydrophobic phosphate group is a hydrophobic molecule
options.B: contains one glycerol molecule contains three glycerol molecules
options.C: fewer ester bonds more ester bonds
options.D: more fatty acids fewer fatty acids

questions.questionText: Adult human haemoglobin typically consists of two  chains and two  chains. Approximately 5% of humans have one amino acid in the  chain that has been changed. This change affects the structure and stability of haemoglobin. Which levels of protein structure could be affected in the haemoglobin of the humans with the changed amino acid?

options.A: primary only

questions.questionText: Lysozyme occurs in human tears, saliva, milk and mucus. Lysozyme has a role in the immune system and hydrolyses peptidoglycan. Which description of lysozyme is correct?

options.A: It is an extracellular antibody.
options.C: It is an extracellular antibacterial protein.
options.D: It is an intracellular antibacterial protein.

questions.questionText: Which letter in the flow diagram shows the effect of adding a competitive inhibitor to an enzyme-catalysed reaction? is a reversible reaction yes no affects the V value affects the K value max m of the enzyme of the enzyme yes no yes no

options.A: B C D

questions.questionText: The cell surface membrane structure is described as a ‘fluid mosaic’. Which statement describes the ‘mosaic’ part of the cell surface membrane?

options.A: the different patterns that are obtained by the moving phospholipid molecules
options.B: the random distribution of cholesterol molecules within the phospholipid bilayer
options.C: the regular pattern produced by the phospholipid heads and membrane proteins
options.D: the scattering of the different proteins within the phospholipid bilayer

questions.questionText: Solute X is at a higher concentration outside a cell than in the cytoplasm. Which processes may allow solute X to be moved through the cell surface membrane?

options.A: active transport, diffusion and facilitated diffusion

options.A: The ratio decreases by a quarter.

questions.questionText: Bacteria were grown in a medium containing 15N. After several generations, all of the DNA contained 15N. Some of these bacteria were transferred to a medium containing the common isotope of nitrogen, 14N. The bacteria were allowed to divide once. The DNA of some of these bacteria was extracted and analysed. This DNA was all hybrid DNA containing equal amounts of 14N and 15N (14N/15N). In another experiment, some bacteria from the medium with 15N were transferred into a medium of 14N. The bacteria were allowed to divide three times. The DNA of some of these bacteria was extracted and analysed. What is the composition of this DNA?

options.A: B 100 100 75 75 percentage percentage 50 50 of DNA of DNA

options.C: D 100 100 75 75 percentage percentage 50 50 of DNA of DNA

questions.questionText: A molecule of transfer RNA (tRNA) has the anticodon sequence UAC. What will be the corresponding nucleotide sequence in the DNA?

options.A: ATG B AUG C TAC D TUG

questions.questionText: The diameter of a tree trunk usually decreases slightly during the day and increases slightly at night. Which three environmental factors, if increased, could cause the largest decrease in diameter?

options.A: humidity, temperature, wind speed

questions.questionText: Sucrose moves within a phloem sieve tube from a source to a sink by mass flow. Which type of gradient within the phloem sieve tube between the source and sink causes the movement of sucrose?

options.A: diffusion gradient

questions.questionText: What effect does decreasing carbon dioxide concentration have on haemoglobin?

options.A: It is less efficient at taking up oxygen and less efficient at releasing oxygen.
options.B: It is less efficient at taking up oxygen and more efficient at releasing oxygen.
options.C: It is more efficient at taking up oxygen and less efficient at releasing oxygen.
options.D: It is more efficient at taking up oxygen and more efficient at releasing oxygen.

questions.questionText: Why does the red blood cell count increase in humans as they start living at high altitude?

options.A: to allow more carbon dioxide to be excreted by the lungs, preventing a fall in blood pH
options.B: to allow more oxygen to be taken up by the haemoglobin as the partial pressure of oxygen is lower
options.C: to allow more oxygen to be taken up by the lungs as there is a lower percentage of oxygen in the air
options.D: to allow more oxygen to be transported as the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen is lowered

questions.questionText: The diagrams show the result of incubating two species of bacteria, P and R, on separate Petri dishes each containing nutrient agar. Three filter paper discs have been added to each Petri dish. bacteria N N key N = no antibiotic X = antibiotic X X Y X Y Y = antibiotic Y bacteria P bacteria R Which statement is correct?

questions.questionText: The statements are about infectious diseases.

Muscle cells have cell surface receptors for the neurotransmitter, ACh. These receptors allow the muscle to respond to a nerve impulse. In the condition myasthenia gravis, the helper T cells stimulate a clone of B cells to become plasma cells and secrete antibodies that bind to and block these ACh receptors. The muscles cannot be stimulated and begin to break down.

options.A: antibodies that bind to ACh receptors
options.C: plasma cells secreting anti-ACh receptor antibodies

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the simplified structure of an antibody. X U V W Which statement is correct?

options.A: U and X allow the antibody to bind to two different antigens.
options.B: V allows the antibody to fit around the antigen.
options.C: W can bind to one specific antigen.
options.D: X can bind with a specific phagocyte receptor.

questions.questionText: Why have vaccination programmes eradicated smallpox but not TB?

options.A: Vaccination can provide immunity only for smallpox but not for TB.
options.B: Only TB is associated with poor living conditions.
options.C: The smallpox virus showed little variation of antigens.
